title: TracePoint safety policy
description: The envelope a human grants. Supplied with --policy, TRACEPOINT_POLICY or individual flags, and fixed for the lifetime of a server. A configuration's safety section can only tighten this; anything looser is refused with POLICY_DENIED and exit 2, naming exactly what a human must change. Agents cannot raise a policy.

allow_targets.description: Hosts, IP addresses or CIDRs that may be targeted even when they resolve to public addresses. Loopback, private and link-local addresses are allowed without listing. Every target host is resolved before load starts and checked against this list.

deny_targets.description: Hosts, IP addresses or CIDRs that are never allowed, even if they are private or appear in allow_targets. Checked first.

allow_public_targets.description: Allow any public address without listing it. Off by default: pointing a load generator at an arbitrary public host is how a test becomes an attack.

allow_writes.description: Permit SQL statements and Redis commands classified as writes.

allow_dangerous.description: Permit destructive or administrative statements. Implies nothing about allow_writes; both are required for a destructive write.

allow_detach.description: Permit background runs (run --detach and the start_run operation).

max_rate_per_runner.description: Ceiling on offered operations per second for any single runner.

max_in_flight.description: Ceiling on concurrent in-flight operations for any single runner.

max_duration.description: Ceiling on run.duration, as a Go duration string.

max_concurrent_runs.description: How many runs may be active at once. Two tests against one target measure each other.

run_root.description: Directory run directories are created under. Servers refuse paths outside it.

redact_headers.description: Additional header names whose values are redacted everywhere. Authorization, Cookie, Set-Cookie, Proxy-Authorization and X-Api-Key are always redacted.
